prompt: Human: How do you take a hearing test?
response:
The process depends a bit on the type of hearing test you’re getting.  You’ll probably be asked to perform a simple action, like tapping your foot on a table as your audiologist or doctor listens for the clicking.  Or you might be asked to read a sequence of numbers aloud, or to perform a bit of finger tapping or other simple finger movements that your audiologist or doctor can compare to sounds you make with your mouth or nose.  If it’s a dexterity test, you might need to do several things in succession, like turn your hand over and under.  Auditory tests usually involve a person tapping their nose, although you might also be asked to blow softly into a bottle or cup as your audiologist listens for clicks.  If it’s a simple tone hearing test, you’ll be asked to hit a note on a piano or other instrument, then to move your finger up and down on the piano.  Some tests will involve moving your arm or hand up and down.  If it’s a complex hearing test, you might need to read text aloud from a phone, or to play a list of notes on a piano, then repeat what you hear and make appropriate notes.  Also, some tests involve you performing a simple action, like holding a piece of wax in your mouth while you listen to sounds, or tapping your foot or hand on a table and counting as your ears listen for the clicks.  In the vast majority of cases, an audiologist or doctor will do everything by ear.  They’ll listen for clicks and sounds that you’re making and note which ones are similar to the sounds they hear in your ears and which are different.

And one last thing, some people get their hearing tested with a “baked bean test”.  They take a piece of white foam that’s similar in consistency to a baked bean and blow it into your ear canal.  The sound of the foam is compared to sounds your ears hear and you can get an idea of the hearing loss.  The reason this works is that the foam will get lodged in the tiny airholes and passages in your outer ears, so you won’t be able to hear the same sounds from other places in your head.
